strings: Planting the Heart is a task undertaken for the herbalist Denalan by the shores of Lake Al'Ameth in Teldrassil. After stripping away the suffocating moss from a strange wooden heart taken from a corrupted timberling, Denalan tests whether his specially enriched soil can cleanse and heal the lingering taint within it.

While examining the strange wooden organ recovered from the corrupted timberling known as Blackmoss the Fetid, Denalan manages to scrape away the foul moss strangling its surface. Yet despite his efforts, a deeper, unnatural taint still pulses within the wood. Rather than burn or discard it, Denalan relies on his lifelong craft of botany and soil tending. He instructs travelers to bury the heart directly into his personal planter box, trusting the rich nutrients he blended to coax whatever natural vitality remains back toward health.

Placing the blackened wooden heart into Denalan's planter yields an unexpected reaction. The moment it touches the fertile soil, the heart burrows into the dirt as if guided by primal instinct. Moments later, it re-emerges to the surface, cleansed of its foul corruption and pulsing with a gentle, companionable warmth. By purifying the seed of a fallen, tainted creature, Denalan demonstrates that even when the wild denizens of Teldrassil fall prey to unnatural blights, careful nurturing and sacred earth can still restore harmony.
Where does this tainted heart come from?
The heart originally came from Blackmoss the Fetid, a corrupted timberling lurking along the shores of Lake Al'Ameth. It was recovered choked with tangled, foul moss before Denalan scraped it clean.
heart origin | where did the heart come from | blackmoss heart

Denalan is a night elf botanist and herbalist who tends an isolated camp on the eastern edge of Lake Al'Ameth. He spends his days studying Teldrassil's plant life, investigating the strange corruption creeping through the boughs, and mixing enriched soils.
Why put the heart in a planter instead of destroying it?

Denalan believes in understanding and healing nature rather than merely destroying corrupted beings. He hopes the nutritive soil he prepared can purge the taint and restore the heart's original, pure vitality.
why plant the heart | why heal the heart
What happens when you bury the heart?
The heart immediately burrows into the soil upon contact. Seconds later, it wriggles back to the surface completely cleansed of its foul taint, pulsing gently as an animated companion.
what happens in the planter | heart burrows
Does this cure the corruption of the timberlings?

It cures only this single salvaged heart. While it proves that individual botanical spirits can be cleansed with care and rich soil, the overarching corruption spreading across Teldrassil remains an active danger.
Why is the soil in Denalan's planter special?
Denalan has spent considerable time experimenting with compost and nutritive soil blends around Lake Al'Ameth, designing dirt potent enough to revitalize sickly flora and purge creeping decay.

For a druid, witnessing a corrupted timberling's core cleansed through rich earth offers a reassuring sign that the unnatural taint afflicting the World Tree's boughs can still be turned back through natural care.
Denalan's mastery over nutrient-rich soil and botanical rejuvenation showcases the vital link between studying the earth and mending damaged plant life.
Restoring living wood and coaxing life from fallen forest spirits reflects the kaldorei commitment to stewarding nature even in the face of Teldrassil's troubling ailments.

This quest bridges an excavation mystery from Darkshore across the Great Sea to the Wetlands. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker entrusts you with a strange Kalimdor fossil, directing you to Archaeologist Flagongut in Menethil Harbor to unlock its secrets.

While examining the strange fossil uncovered in Darkshore, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker notices a striking resemblance to a relic shown at an Explorers' League conference back in Ironforge. That earlier piece was presented by Archaeologist Flagongut, who was convinced that such fossils held latent powers waiting to be unlocked. Greywhisker believes Flagongut is the only dwarf capable of discerning what makes this Kalimdor find so extraordinary.

Carrying the mysterious relic means undertaking a long journey out of Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms. Flagongut was last seen waiting for an armed escort to the Whelgar Excavation Site while lodging at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Delivering the fossil into his hands marks the turning point where a local Darkshore survey ties into a continent-spanning archaeological inquiry.

This quest marks the final chapter in the search sparked by Prospector Remtravel's excavations in Darkshore. Archaeologist Flagongut in Menethil Harbor seeks to combine Remtravel's finds with his own fossil and the lost Stone of Relu to unlock the ancient relics' hidden powers.

What began as an escort mission aiding the distracted Prospector Remtravel in the northern reaches of Darkshore leads across the Great Sea to the marshlands of the Wetlands. Flagongut's own original fossil is held by Prospector Whelgar at his excavation site in the Wetlands. Archaeologist Flagongut, reviewing the collected finds, realizes that unlocking the mysterious powers within the fossils requires a key artifact: the Stone of Relu.

Before Flagongut could rendezvous with Whelgar, a pack of mottled raptors ambushed his caravan along the road, devouring the Stone of Relu. To piece the mystery together, Flagongut requires an adventurer to hunt down the predatory beasts, recover the ingested stone, and retrieve the original fossil from Whelgar's camp. With both fossils and the key assembled, the dwarven researchers hope to uncover the relics' true origin and power.

The Call of Earth is a sacred trial overseen by Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar, testing initiates in the patience and resilience of stone. Aspirants must confront the Frostmane trolls to the south to claim their bear pendants before being granted an earthen sapta.

At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, the mentor Teo Hammerstorm watches over initiates ready to walk the rugged path of the earth. Viewing the land as a stout and unyielding foundation, Teo guides young wanderers to heed the wisdom of the mountains. He warns that while stone serves as an enduring shield, its favor is not given lightly, requiring true grit and deep respect before any secrets of the soil will be shared.

To demonstrate readiness, an initiate must face the Frostmane trolls lurking in a cave to the south. These trolls fashion coarse pendants from the ferocious Iceclaw bears that roam the frozen heights. Reclaiming two of these bear pendants from the troll den serves as tangible proof that the petitioner possesses the stubborn resolve and fortitude expected by the elemental spirits.

Upon presenting the pendants to Teo Hammerstorm, the elder commends the initiate's patience—the earth's finest virtue, which outlasts crumbling peaks and carved river valleys. In recognition of this proven respect, Teo sets to work preparing an earthen sapta, an essential catalyst enabling the initiate to perceive and walk the true path of the elements.

Because of its potency, the draught must only be consumed in a designated holy site where the bond between spirit and stone can safely take hold.
The Spirit Stone in the Snow

High up a snow-swept mountain, tucked away at the terminus of a secluded hidden path, rests the Spirit Stone. Initiates journey into this bitter, frozen landscape to stand humbly before the ancient rock. By presenting themselves without pride and imbibing the sapta, they discover that even in the harshest winter crags, the living earth extends its welcome. The mountains become a foundation of enduring physical strength, while the vast, steady plains teach the quiet power of patience.

Communing with stone serves as a foundational rite for spiritual pathfinders. Unlike the restless fury of wind, fire, or crashing water, the earth teaches unmoving discipline and quiet resilience. To pass the rite, the seeker must absorb the earth's quiet essence, preparing their mind and body for the conflicting, chaotic dualities of the more volatile elements that roar across the world.

This quest sends Alliance adventurers south across Darkshore to scout the eerie Master's Glaive on behalf of the ancient of lore, Onu. The goal is to investigate whether the sinister Twilight's Hammer cult has infiltrated the remains of the fallen ancient horror.

While investigating the lingering corruption and displaced wildlife along Darkshore, the ancient of lore Onu notices alarming clues. The naga along the coast are troubled enough, but the presence of the Twilight's Hammer cult is far more ominous. This fanatic sect does not worship ordinary dark powers; they venerate the ancient, primal lords of the world who were overthrown in ages past.

Southward lies the Master's Glaive, a grim excavation centered around a colossal creature impaled by an immense stone weapon. Onu provides a Phial of Scrying and tasks scouts with entering the pit to confirm if the cultists have gathered there. As Onu warns, even though the impaled behemoth has been dead for eons, slivers of its ancient, corruptive power still linger within its bones—a prize the Twilight's Hammer cannot resist.

Meddlesome Mages centers on rising friction in the Shen'dar Highlands, where apprentices of the High Order trespass near sacred standing stones. Local guardians must drive them away to protect the delicate mystical forces that hold their island together from reckless arcane tampering.

Despite repeated warnings to leave these sacred sites undisturbed, the mages have pressed forward with their arcane interests. The local leadership, though hesitant to shed the blood of their shen'dorei kin, has called for outside intervention to disperse the encroaching apprentices before their interference causes permanent harm.

The urgency behind driving off the High Order stems from the delicate balance that sustains the island. The mystical forces binding the land together are fragile, leaving the homeland vulnerable to reckless spellcraft. To the defenders of the standing stones, the High Order demonstrates complete disregard for the dangers of their meddling, meaning even a single careless spell could rupture the island's bindings and bring ruin upon all who dwell there.

A Magical Affront is a quest on Zephras centering on a clash over recently surfaced leylines. While a local order seeks to harness and study the exposed arcane energies, the Windshapers view the breaches as scars upon the earth that must be healed, sparking direct conflict in the southwestern forest.

On the surface of Zephras, ancient subterranean conduits of raw magic have recently broken through the earth. For the scholars and practitioners of the local order, this emergence is an invaluable boon. Direct, tangible contact with the leylines grants them unprecedented insight into the arcane currents that permeate the region, vastly expanding their magical mastery.

Not everyone regards the exposed energies as a miracle. The Windshapers view the breaches as open wounds and destructive scars torn across the face of Zephras. Determined to heal the wounded earth, they gather at the rupture sites to suppress or mend the exposed leylines. To the order relying on that raw power, this interference is an intolerable threat, prompting them to send adventurers southwest into the forest to drive the Windshapers back.
